supporting_observations.claim: At 13:35 UTC, WS-ESTONE-01 recorded a Windows event 4648 in which SYSTEM used explicit credentials for svc-billing, targeting DC-PIN-01 via PowerShell.
At 13:27 UTC, DC-PIN-01 recorded a Windows event 4648 in which SYSTEM used explicit credentials for svc-billing, targeting FILE-PIN-01 via PowerShell.
These event 4648 records show explicit-credential use, but do not establish whether authentication succeeded or failed; they are not sufficient to confirm the alert's reported repeated failed logons.

known_telemetry_limitations: Windows security and Sysmon logs were not collected from DC-PIN-01 and FILE-PIN-01 from 13:30 through 14:15 UTC, overlapping the alert period and scheduled password rotation.
The supplied records do not include authentication outcome details for the explicit-credential events.
claims_not_established: Whether svc-billing actually had repeated failed domain logons around 13:40 UTC.
Whether the 13:35 credential use from WS-ESTONE-01 was authorized as part of the scheduled password rotation or job update.
What commands or script content ran in PowerShell, who initiated the activity, or whether credentials were exposed or misused.
Whether the activity resulted in successful access to DC-PIN-01 or FILE-PIN-01.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover or obtain DC-PIN-01 and FILE-PIN-01 authentication and process logs for 13:30–14:15 UTC, including logon outcomes and relevant account-management events.
Review WS-ESTONE-01 process and PowerShell records around 13:35 UTC to identify the script, command line, initiating user, and reason for using svc-billing credentials.
Verify the svc-billing password rotation and BillingSync job update records, including who performed them and when.
Check whether the reported failed-logon alert has underlying event records, with source host, timestamps, and authentication outcomes.
